idiom_name: Prettier printWidth/tabWidth plus ESLint no-else-return and curly
implementation_notes: In JavaScript the rectangle is whatever Prettier prints: it rewrites every file to a fixed print width (80 by default) with a two-space indent step, which draws the block shape and enforces the width discipline that the pattern wants - long branches must be extracted because Prettier will otherwise wrap them arbitrarily. ESLint carries the depth half: no-else-return removes the else after an early return, and curly (or the project's equivalent) decides whether a single-statement body gets braces. Hand-formatting is justified only in a project that deliberately has no formatter; then keep the existing file's shape rather than introducing a new one.
pitfalls: Prettier explodes long expressions: a deep call chain inside a branch gets wrapped across lines and the right edge of the rectangle disappears unless the expression is extracted into a named const.
Running Prettier and ESLint's indent rule together makes the two tools fight over continuation lines; use eslint-config-prettier or drop the indent rule instead of maintaining two layouts.
Optional chaining and nested ternaries compress a decision into one line that is technically rectangular but hides its branches; the depth budget still applies.
